9.5.9. qnav.gravity.ggm_plus

9.5.9.1. ggm_plus.py

summary:

Global Gravity Map Plus (GGMPlus) gravity map implementations. This module provides support for the GGMPlus gravity models. Specifically, two implementations for the GGPlus gravity acceleration and gravity disturbance corrections.

author:

Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk

version:

1.0.0 - First implementation of this module.

class qnav.gravity.ggm_plus.GGMPlusAcc(base_model: GravityModel, geoid_model: GeoidModel | None, map_dir: Path, auto_download: bool = True, margin_size: int = 1)[source]

Global Gravity Map Plus for Acceleration Correction. An implementation of GGMPlus, using the provided base gravity acceleration values. This overwrites the base values zero-altitude gravity estimation, but uses its altitude extrapolation.

calc_gravity_z(lat: float, lon: float, alt: float) → float[source]

Calculates and returns the total gravitational acceleration. Computes the gravity along the Z/Down axis (in m/s^2) for the given location and altitude offset.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinate for the position of interest. The latitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate for the position of interest. The longitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • alt (float) – The altitude offset for the position of interest. The elevation from the WGS-84 reference ellipsoid in metres.

Returns:

The downwards gravitational acceleration for each location.

Return type:

float

calc_gravity_z_vec(lat: ndarray, lon: ndarray, alt: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

In a vectorised batch, calculates and returns the gravitational acceleration along the Z/Down axis (in m/s^2) for the given location and altitude offset. Ideal when calculating gravity for a large number of positions.

Parameters:

  • lat (np.array) – The latitude coordinate for the position of interest. The latitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • lon (np.array) – The longitude coordinate for the position of interest. The longitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • alt (np.array) – The altitude offset for the position of interest. The elevation from the WGS-84 reference ellipsoid in metres.

Returns:

The downwards gravitational acceleration for each location (in m/s^2).

Return type:

np.array (N-elements)

get_anomaly(lat: float, lon: float) → float[source]

Calculates the gravity anomaly for given position. Retrieves the gravity anomaly value for the requested position (in m/s^2) at the base surface. For gravity maps this value is interpolated from its dataset, following possible conversion.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinate for the position of interest. The latitude position value given in decimal degrees.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate for the position of interest. The longitude position value given in decimal degrees.

Returns:

The gravity anomaly value (in m/s^2).

Return type:

float

get_anomaly_vec(lat: ndarray, lon: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Calculates the gravity anomaly for multiple given positions. Retrieves the gravity anomaly value for the requested position (in m/s^2) at the base surface. For gravity maps this value is interpolated from its dataset, following possible conversion.

Parameters:

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate for the position of interest. The longitude position value given in decimal degrees.

Return type:

float

get_map_value(lat: float, lon: float) → float[source]

Interpolates the gravity acceleration for requested position(. Looks-up and returns the gravity anomaly value for requested latitude and longitude position.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinate in decimal degrees.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate in decimal degrees.

Returns:

The interpolated gravity map value in m/s^2.

Return type:

float

get_map_values(lat: ndarray, lon: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Looks-up the correction values using the map. This will dynamically load data to cover the range, keeping the maximum number of loaded tiles under the margin value, to conserve memory constraints.

Parameters:

  • lat (np.ndarray) – The latitude coordinate in decimal degrees.

  • lon (np.ndarray) – The longitude coordinate in decimal degrees.

Returns:

The corresponding values interpolated from the map.

Return type:

np.ndarray

download_data(origin_lat: int, origin_lon: int, overwrite: bool = False)[source]

Downloads the required marine gravity files from the source. If allowed and files are not present, will download the required geosat files to the set directory. Optionally, files can be overwritten.

Parameters:

  • origin_lat (int) – Origin latitude of tile to download.

  • origin_lon (int) – Origin longitude of tile to download.

  • overwrite (bool) – Should downloading replace existing files. By default this is set to false and only missing files are downloaded.

class qnav.gravity.ggm_plus.GGMPlusDist(base_model: GravityModel, geoid_model: GeoidModel | None, map_dir: Path, auto_download: bool = True, margin_size: int = 1)[source]

qnav.gravity.ggm_plus.read_ggm_file(file_path: Path) → ndarray[source]

Reads the data from a given GGM_plus file. Once read, the returned 2500-by-2500 matrix data will be in \(metres/second^2\). No latitude or longitude coordinates are contained within any GGM_plus file.

Parameters:

file_path (Path or str) – The location of the GGM_plus file to read.

Returns:

The gravitational acceleration matrix read from the file, measured in \(metres/second^2\)

Return type:

NumPy Matrix (2500-by-2500 elements)

qnav.gravity.ggm_plus.get_empty_ggm_tile() → ndarray[source]

Produces an empty tile of dimensions of GGM Plus data file. Used when data is unavailable and cannot be downloaded.

Returns:

Empty GGM Plus tile data for missing files.

Return type:

NumPy Matrix (2500-by-2500 elements)
